title: storytold/wordcraft
why_read: An ambitious clean-room reimplementation of Microsoft Word in Rust is a serious engineering challenge worth examining for document format and rendering internals.
analysis: Rebuilding a word processor from scratch, especially one aiming for compatibility with Word's complex document model, formatting engine, and file formats, is a substantial systems engineering undertaking. Doing it in Rust suggests attention to performance and memory safety, which is relevant for engineers interested in text layout engines, rich text editing, or binary/XML document format parsing (like .docx). The 'clean-room' framing implies the implementation was built without referencing Microsoft's actual source, which is notable from both a legal and reverse-engineering perspective. This is the kind of project that reveals a lot about the hidden complexity of software that looks simple on the surface.
